title: Brown butter shortbread
subtitle: classic Scottish shortbread made with beurre noisette for a nutty, caramel depth
excerpt: Brown butter shortbread uses beurre noisette (butter cooked until the milk solids turn golden and nutty) in place of plain butter. The difference is noticeable: the finished biscuit has the same sandy, crumbling texture of classic shortbread but with a deeper, more complex flavour. The brown butter must be chilled until solid before use.
sourceNotes: Brown butter shortbread, a contemporary development on the classic Scottish shortbread (documented in Scottish cookbooks from the eighteenth century). Beurre noisette method from standard British and French patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Butter cooked over a medium heat until the water evaporates and the milk solids toast to a golden-brown, giving a nutty, caramel aroma. From the French for hazelnut butter, because of its colour and smell.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked, cooled shortbread in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: The butter is first turned into

, then chilled until solid and used as you would regular butter. Do not rush the browning: the butter should turn golden-amber and smell nutty, not burnt. Watch the colour in the pan and remove from the heat the moment the milk solids are a deep hazelnut shade.

Melt the butter in a small light-coloured saucepan over a medium heat. It will foam, then subside. Continue cooking, swirling the pan occasionally, for about 5 minutes until the milk solids at the base of the pan turn golden-brown and the butter smells nutty.

Pour immediately into a bowl (leave any very dark specks in the pan). Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until solid, about 1 hour. The chilled brown butter should be the consistency of regular cold butter.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Line a 20 cm square tin with baking parchment.
Beat the solid brown butter and caster sugar together until pale and soft. Add the vanilla extract. Mix in the flour and salt until the dough comes together. It will be stiff.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared tin. Prick all over with a fork. Sprinkle with granulated sugar if using. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until pale golden and fully cooked through. The shortbread should not be brown on top. Score into fingers while still warm in the tin, then leave to cool completely before removing.

attrs.problem: Butter burnt and acrid rather than nutty
attrs.avoid: Avoid high heat; the milk solids burn quickly once the butter stops foaming.
attrs.fix: Use medium heat and watch the colour constantly from the moment the foaming subsides. Discard burnt butter and start again.

attrs.problem: Shortbread crumbly and falling apart when cut
attrs.avoid: Avoid cutting when fully cold; shortbread scored while warm holds its shape better.
attrs.fix: Score the shortbread in the tin while still warm (about 10 minutes after coming out of the oven), then leave to cool completely before lifting out.
